Tax Relief | Representative Mike Carey After years of stubborn inflation, American families and small businesses need tax relief to make ends meet today and plan for tomorrow. As a member of the House Ways & Means Committee, I have the privilege of working on tax policy that will impact every household and business in the country. In my role with the committee, I supported extending and expanding necessary tax relief to life up American middle-class families, increase jobs, and increase affordable housing across the country by supporting the House-passed Tax Relief for Americans Workers and Families Act . We are also tasked renewing the tax cuts established in the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act , which inspired job creation and business investment that is the envy of the world. In lead up to the expiration of certain tax provision in TCJA, Ways & Means Chairman Jason Smith formed 10 Committee Tax Teams . These teams are tasked with identifying legislative solutions to help families, workers, and small businesses that are currently struggling due to staggering inflation. I have been assigned to the Community Development, American Workforce, and Working Families tax teams. Community Development will focus on policies such as the Historic Tax Credit, and the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit. American Workforce is focusing on the tax policy to develop policies to protect and support American workforce. The Working Families team will focus on tax provisions to support families that are currently facing financial challenges with inflation and the rising costs of daily living. Strengthening America's Workforce | Representative Mike Carey Made in America isn’t just a slogan: it’s recipe for a stronger, more prosperous future. The first step? Investing in good-paying jobs here at home, in fields ranging from manufacturing to tech to energy production. We’ve been pleased to welcome great employers to Ohio’s Fifteenth District, like Honda’s $3.5 billion battery plant in Fayette County that created an estimated 2,200 new jobs. Our district has also received $2.3 billion investment from Google in the form of three new data centers in Columbus, Lancaster and New Albany. Investing in America should be good for business. That’s why we’ve supported legislation to prevent U.S. trade policy from favoring foreign e-commerce. In our work with the Ways and Means Committee, we also passed the Tax Relief for American Families and Workers Act . This will restore crucial research and development expensing so that American businesses can invest in their next big idea. We’re also working to build the next generation of America’s workforce. We supported the bipartisan Leveraging and Energizing America’s Apprenticeship Programs Act to give tax incentives to businesses who hire apprentices. This legislation will develop the careers of skilled workers in industries from construction to healthcare to manufacturing. Workers should feel that they have a voice in Washington. We have been active on efforts to protect workers, like the Coordination of Medicare Payments and Workers’ Compensation Act, or the COMP ACT , which aims to protect injured workers whose compensation claims overlap with Medicare coverage. Housing Affordability | Representative Mike Carey Stable, affordable housing is increasingly out of reach for too many. We’re working give hardworking families their shot at the American dream. In a 2021 survey, 70 percent of Americans say that young adults today have a harder time buying a home than their parents’ generation did. It’s no wonder why: in 2023, just 15.5 percent of homes on the market were affordable for a typical U.S. household. In Ohio, nearly 400,000 people spend more than half of their monthly income on housing. The ability to comfortably afford a home allows us to lay down the roots that can grow a family, career, and a community. That’s why it’s a top priority to increase Americans’ access to affordable housing. We were proud to introduce the Workforce Housing Tax Credit Act , which will establish the first-ever middle-income housing tax credit, which is expected to finance 344,000 affordable rental homes. Along with our colleagues on the House Ways and Means Committee, we were also strong supporters of the Tax Relief for American Families and Workers Act, which expanded the Low-Income Housing Tax Credit from 9 percent to 12.5 percent. Since 1986, this credit has preserved nearly 13,000 units of affordable housing in the 15th district. Supporting Working Families | Representative Mike Carey As a dad and grandpa, I know how challenging it can be for families to make ends meet. That’s why we are proud to lead on legislation that allows families to thrive. This means investing in their ability to save, plan for the future, and care for those they love. For example: approximately 1.46 million Ohioans are family caregivers for loved ones at home and in nursing facilities, young and old. Our bipartisan, bicameral Credit for Caring Act would help cover more than $7,200 of out-of-pocket costs that families spend on caregiving costs including home care aides, adult day care, respite care, transportation and more. Watch: Carey speaks in support of his Youth Poisoning Protection Act We’re also working to keep kids safe and their parents supported, particularly with rising rates of mental illness impacting young people. Our Youth Poisoning Protection Act , which passed the House, would keep deadly poisons out of the hands of vulnerable young people. Additionally, our Promoting Community-Based Prevention Services Act would encourage the funding for family resource centers. These centers provide mental health and addiction resources along with many other vital services for families in need. Affordability, worsened by persistent inflation, is a major challenge for many Ohio families. As a member of the House Committee on Ways and Means, we were proud to support the Tax Relief for American Workers and Families Act. This bill expanded and strengthened the Child Tax Credit by making more of a taxpayer’s income eligible for the credit and removing the penalty for families with multiple children. Domestic Energy Independence | Representative Mike Carey All-of-the-above energy, produced here at home, will bring down consumer prices, end dependence on our adversaries for key resources and safeguard our national security. We’ve been hard at work in Congress to unleash American energy independence. The first step: making it easier to harness our energy resources. Our Promoting Domestic Energy Production Act will treat the oil and gas industry like other capital intensive industries, allowing producers to deduct their Intangible Drilling Costs (IDCs). IDCs make up 85 percent of the initial investment in oil exploration and well development, and mainly consist of labor costs. Allowing producers to deduct IDCs will free up funds for them to reinvest in development and job creation. We’re also working to reduce burdensome energy costs. Our Pay Less at the Pump Act would eliminate the Hazard Substance Superfund Financing on crude oil imports. By ending this tax, Americans will save an estimated $10.5 billion over the next ten years. As we support an all-of-the-above future, we must ensure that taxpayer funds are being spent responsibly in the process. Our Clean Energy Demonstration Transparency Act , which passed the House with bipartisan support, will provide much-needed oversight to the Department of Energy’s Office of Clean Energy Demonstration. In 2021, the Department of Energy blew their budget by more than $300 million on a clean energy project, designing four facilities which were never actually built. We were proud to lead on this common-sense legislation to protect taxpayer dollars and support all-of-the-above energy independence.
